issues.description: The return type of Stock.getStockIngredients differs between the template and the solution repositories. In the template, getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient>, while in the solution it returns StockIngredient[]. This is a structural mismatch that can confuse students comparing the solution to the provided template (or expecting a consistent API for Stock).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of getStockIngredients consistent across template and solution. Choose either List<StockIngredient> or StockIngredient[] and update both repositories and any code that consumes this method (e.g., Main or tests) to use the chosen type.

issues.description: Within the template Stock class, the setter and getter use different types: setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) takes an array, but getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient>. This internal inconsistency in the template API may confuse students about the intended representation and usage of stock ingredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter and setter use the same type in the template. Either change getStockIngredients() to return StockIngredient[] to match setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]), or change setStockIngredients to accept a List<StockIngredient>. Keep the chosen representation consistent across the project.
